Senses.Explanation: Tianlong’s one finger names the inherited case in which Tianlong raises one finger and Juzhi claims lifelong use of the received one-finger Chan. Later collections retell and criticize that transmission. A single raised finger becomes an inherited public response whose very transmission is tested by later threats to break it off. The table-of-contents occurrence was rejected as containment; only the two full retellings support this provisional case-label entry. Tianlong’s gesture and Juzhi’s claimed reception form one inherited finger case, not two unrelated fingers.
